1 1.

Briefly stated, the case of the prosecution is that on 17.01.2019 at about 11:00 AM,
at Jeevan Park Bus stand, accused Anil along with co-accused cheated the complainant and took his two gold finger rings and thereby committed the offences punishable under Sections 420/34/120B of IPC for which FIR no. 28/2019 was registered at the police station Janakpuri, New Delhi.
INVESTIGATION AND APPEARANCE OF ACCUSED 2.

After registration of the FIR, the Investigating Officer (hereinafter, "IO") undertook investigation and on culmination of the same, the charge-sheet against the accused person, namely, Anil was filed.
The Court took the cognizance against the accused person and summons were issued to the accused.
On his appearance, a copy of the charge-sheet was supplied to the accused in terms of section 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter, "CrPC").
On finding a prima facie case against the accused person, charge under Sections 120B/420/34 of IPC was framed against the accused on 06.08.2019.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 3.

During the trial, prosecution led the following oral and documentary evidence against the accused to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt: -

To prove its case, prosecution examined the following witnesses, the same are as follows:
5.

PW1 Robert Massey deposed that on 17.01.2019 at around 12 noon near bus stop,
Jeewan Park, he had gone to the bus stop to purchase medicine for his mother and as he was standing at a distance from the bus top, he saw two boys coming from front.
One of the boys stood near him and the other threw handkerchief on his face.
Thereafter, PW1 became unconscious and the same person get water for him.
After some time, when the PW1 regained consciousness, he found out that his two gold rings were missing.
Thereafter, PW-1 along with his son went to PS Janakpuri and lodged a complaint and the same is Ex. PW 1/A.

PW-1 went to the spot with PW-2 IO SI Raj Kumar and at the instance of the PW-1 site plan was prepared and the same is Ex.PW1/B.
6.
PW2 Rtd.
SI Raj Kumar deposed that on 17.01.2019, he was posted as SI at PS Jankpuri and PW1 Robert Massey came to the PS and filed complaint which is Ex.PW1/A.
Thereafter, he prepared Tehrir which is Ex.PW2/A and handed over the same to DO for registration of FIR.

He further submitted that site plan was prepared during the investigation at the instance of the complainant State v. Anil FIR no.
28/2019 page 3 of 10 Digitally signed by HARJOT HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.07.09 16:58:24 +0545 which is Ex.PW1/B.
He also submitted that no CCTV camera was found installed at the spot.
Thereafter, the investigation was transferred to ASI Satish.
7. PW3 Rtd.
SI Satish Kumar deposed that on 23.01.2019, he was posted at PS Janakpuri as ASI.

He submitted that on that day, investigation of the present case was marked to him by the SHO and during investigation on 22.02.2019, on receiving DD No. 25B, HC Ved Prakash, Special Staff informed that accused in the present case has been arrested by him under Kalandara u/s 41.1(d) Cr.P.C dated 21.02.2019.
It is further submitted that thereafter, he went to Special Staff Office, Punjabi Bagh and took the documents of the kalandara and recorded statement of HC Ved Prakash.

He further submitted that thereafter, he reached Dwarka Court and obtained the permission to interrogate and formal arrest of the accused in the present FIR and accused was formally arrested and his disclosure statement was recorded.

He further submitted that thereafter, he moved an application for conducting TIP of the accused but the accused refused to participate in the TIP and thereafter, he moved an application for one day PC remand of accused to trace the co-accused and obtained one day PC remand but co-accused could not be traced.
He further submitted that thereafter, the accused was sent to JC and he prepared the charge sheet and filed the same in Court.

DD writer to prove DD No. 25B dated 22.02.2019 and concerned Ahlmad to prove original DD number dated 21.02.2019 u/s 41.1(d) Cr.P.C and TIP proceedings as Ex.P1, Ex.P2, Ex.P3, Ex.P4 and Ex.A1 respectively.
STATEMENT OF THE ACCUSED AND DEFENCE EVIDENCE 10.

Thereafter, before the start of defence evidence in order to allow the accused person to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against him, the statement of the accused person was recorded on 21.05.2024 without oath under section 281 r/w 313 CrPC, wherein he has stated that he is falsely been implicated in the present case.
He further stated that he did not want to lead defence evidence.
FINAL ARGUMENTS 11.
I have heard the Ld. APP for the State and Ld. Counsel for the accused at length.
I have also given my thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record.
12. It is argued by the Ld. APP for the State that all the ingredients of the offence are fulfilled in the present case.
He has argued that prosecution witnesses have categorically deposed about the commission of offence and there is no ground to disbelieve their testimony.

He further contends that the State v. Anil FIR no. 28/2019 page 5 of 10 Digitally signed by HARJOT HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.07.09 16:58:43 +0545 documentary evidence has proved the offence beyond reasonable doubt.
As such, it is prayed that the accused be punished for the said offences.
13. Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for the accused has argued that the State has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.

The Ld. Counsel further argued that the entire case of the prosecution is false and fabricated and the same is evident from the material inconsistencies and State vs Anil on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5164597/
4 contradictions borne out from the material on record.
It is argued that the prosecution has failed to discharge the burden cast upon it.
As such, it is prayed that the accused be acquitted for the said offence.
INGREDIENTS OF THE OFFENCE 14. Brief, outline of offences for which the accused has been tried are, section 420/120B/34 IPC.

The following Sections are reproduced as follows :
420 IPC. Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property :
"Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."

120B IPC. Punishment of criminal conspiracy :
"(1)Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable with death, imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards, shall, where no express provision is made in this Code for the punishment of such a conspiracy, be punished in the same manner as if he had abetted State v.
Anil FIR no. 28/2019 page 6 of 10 Digitally signed by HARJOT HARJOT SINGH SINGH Date:
2025.07.09 16:58:52 +0545

such offence.(2)Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy to commit an offence punishable as aforesaid shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding six months, or with fine or with both."

34 IPC. Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention :
"When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone."

15. The essential ingredients of offence u/s 420 IPC are :
 i) Deception of any person.
 ii) Fradulent/dishonesh inducement to deliver property.
iii) The inducement must result in wrongful gain to one and  wrongful loss to another.

The essential ingredient of offence u/s 120B IPC are :
i) Agreement between two or more persons.
ii) To do an illegal act or a legal act by illegal means.
iii) The agreement itself is punishable.

17. It is trite law that the burden always lies upon the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of acceptable evidence and that the law does not permit the Court to punish the accused on the basis of moral conviction or on account of suspicion alone.
Also, it is well settled that accused is entitled to the benefit of every reasonable doubt in the prosecution story and such doubt entitles him to acquittal.

sentences.text: +0545  COMPLAINANT'S VERSION 18. PW 1

Robert Massey stated that on 17.01.2019, while he was waiting at Jeewan Park bus stop,
one of two boys threw a handkerchief on his face and he became semi-conscious.
Upon recovery, he found two of his gold rings were missing.
He admitted that he did not see the direction in which the boys fled and could not describe their clothing.
More importantly, he never mentioned any specific identification of the accused at the spot.
ARREST AND TIP PROCEEDINGS 19.
The accused was not apprehended at the spot, nor during investigation of this FIR.
He was arrested by Special Staff on the basis of secret information and a disclosure statement.
TIP was offered but the accused declined to participate.
The refusal of TIP cannot be used adversely when no prior identification or description exists.

sentences.text: PW 1 Robert Massey later identified the accused in court.

However, such in court identification,
without any prior TIP or earlier description, is unsafe and carries little evidentary value.
RECOVERY 21.
No recovery of the alleged stolen gold rings was ever affected from the accused or any co-accused.
There is no independent public witness.
None joined the investigation.
The site of occurence has no CCTV cameras as confirmed by IO PW 2 and PW 3.
No forensic or electronic evidence links the accused to the offence.
State v. Anil FIR no. 28/2019 page 8 of 10
Digitally  signed by  HARJOT  HARJOT SINGH  SINGH

Date:
 2025.07.09  16:59:15  +0545 INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION/POLICE EVIDENCE 22.
PW 2, PW 3 and PW 4 (IOs and arresting officers) confirmed that the accused was not apprehended at the scene of the offence.
The arrest was affected later and was not based on the information of the complainant.
No public witnesses joined the raid and nothing was recovered from the accused.
FINDINGS 23.
The prosecution case hinges solely on the disclosure statement of the accused, which has no evidentary value unless supported by recovery or indenpendent corroboration.

Reference is placed on the judgment titled Pulukuri Kottaya Vs. King Emperor.
24.
No ingredient of criminal conspiracy u/s 120B IPC has been established.
There is no material on record to show prior meeting of minds, agreement or any planning between the accused and any co-offender.
Similarly, the basic ingredients of Section 420 IPC i.e. inducement and dishonest intention from inception are not proved.
There is no evidence of the accused inducing the complainant to part with his property.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show any of the ingredient of Section 34 IPC.
